title: Premarket · Thursday 9/24

headline.title: 753.00 rejected META twice and the event is now over. Tuesday it made 757.27 and closed 736.60. Wednesday it made 763.90 and closed 744.10. Both times through the level, both times back under it. Connect has since delivered — $1,299 Meta VR Glasses and Muse Charm, a handheld that works with Muse, announced late Wednesday — and the stock is −2.03% premarket after nearly +12% on the week.
headline.summary: The tape is selling into the summit, not buying it. Trump–Xi meets in Washington today with the tariff truce, tech restrictions, AI and rare earths all on the agenda — and QQQ is −1.01%, SPY −0.53%. COST reports after the close, the week's last piece of gravity. And VKTX is the lesson of the week: it ran +35.7% Tuesday on obesity data, tagged 43.10 Wednesday, and is −11.88% this morning because the company priced 7.86M shares at $35 plus $225M of 2% converts into its own spike. The data pop was the financing window. That is the pattern, and it is why a +23% gap on trial data had no level worth trading.

overview:
Two sessions since the last report, and the calls mostly held. META: “753.00 up, no trade inside the range” — it never closed above 753 in either session. ONON did exactly what the investor-day study said: gapped to 30.40, ran 31.16, closed 29.39, below its own open. 3 of 5 in that study gapped up and closed below the open, and the note said watch the 9:00 candle, not the gap.

DGX repriced once and held, as a rule change does — 234.76 then 233.00, sitting where the cut put it. SMCI went nowhere, flagged as extended rather than fresh: 41.54 then 41.44.

Two misses, both the same shape. VICR was called a template — license announced, guidance raise is the trade — and then given no entry. It ran +19.85% Tuesday and +5.52% Wednesday, +26.5% in two sessions. XOM was called “not a long here” at 158.30; it bottomed at 155.85 and closed Wednesday 161.23. Being right about direction and giving no level to act on is not being right.

COIN finally tested it. Wednesday's low was 195.64 — through the 196.21 line named Monday for the first time — and it closed 198.13, back above. The level held on its first real test. Premarket 195.65 is back at it.

Crude has turned. WTI bottomed and USO is +1.32%, XOM +1.08%. Gold is breaking the other way — futures hit 4,285.0, the lowest since Sept 16, with KGC −4.13%.

Today: claims 7:30 · new home sales 9:00 · Kansas City Fed 10:00 · Trump–Xi · COST after the close.

prep.pill: MORNING PREP · THU 9/24 · $50 RISK · TRUMP–XI · COST TONIGHT
prep.lead: ⚠ “I am a catalyst trader.” $50 risk. Targeted days, events, extreme volume and earnings. Two dated events today: Trump–Xi in Washington, and COST after the close. Claims 7:30, new home sales 9:00, Kansas City Fed 10:00. The tape is selling into the summit, which is the thing to notice.
cards: META
Twice rejected · −2.03%
r
Tuesday high 757.27, close 736.60. Wednesday high 763.90, close 744.10. Through 753.00 both sessions, back under it both sessions. The level named Tuesday did its whole job.
No long until a close above 763.90. Below 730.00, Tuesday's low, the Muse move is unwinding. Between those two there is nothing to do, same as Tuesday.
Connect has delivered and the stock is red on it. $1,299 Meta VR Glasses and Muse Charm, a handheld that pairs with Muse, both unveiled late Wednesday.
That is sell-the-news after +12% on the week, and it matches the investor-day study's shape: the event arrives, the buyers who front-ran it leave.
The reversal I got wrong Monday and the resistance I got right Tuesday are the same level, four days apart. Structure works once the catalyst is priced — not before it lands.
VKTX
Priced into the spike · −11.88%
r
7.86M shares at $35 plus $225M of 2% converts, upsized, two sessions after +35.7% on obesity data. The company sold into its own news.
$35 is the anchor now — every buyer of that deal owns it there, and premarket 36.70 is barely above. Below $35 the deal is underwater and the sellers have a reason.
This is the pattern worth keeping. A small-cap biotech with a big data print has a financing need, and the spike is when it gets filled. The pop creates the window.
The Monday note said no level to trade against, binary, worst risk-reward on the board. It then ran +35.7% Tuesday and tagged 43.10 Wednesday before this.
Honest ledger: the conclusion was right and it cost a 35% session. That is the trade-off of refusing structureless gaps, and it is the correct one over many trials — not every one.
COST
Reports tonight · +0.58%
y
Fiscal Q4 after the close. The one confirmed earnings date on the board this week and the last scheduled catalyst before MU on 9/30.
★ No position before the print. Wednesday's range 911.29/898.36 is the box it is sitting in. The reaction gap sets the level; trade tomorrow's first thirty minutes, not tonight's headline.
It is drifting up while the index sells off — 909.95 against a 904.70 close with QQQ −1.01%. Relative strength into a print is a real tell.
COST was on the list written a week ago: PATH, ONON, MCD, QCOM, META, COST. Five of the six have now had their event.
Holding premium through a print is a decision to make in advance, not at 2:55. If it is not written down before the close, the answer is no.
VICR
The miss · +26.5% in two
g
+19.85% Tuesday to 268.34, then +5.52% Wednesday to 283.16. From the 223.90 close before the guidance raise, that is +26.5% in two sessions.
Premarket 274.39, −3.10%, first red print of the move. Wednesday's low 261.94 is the first real level this has offered. Chasing 274 after +26.5% is not a setup.
The template was named correctly and then not acted on. The note said: a license announcement is a promise, the guidance raise is the cash, and it arrives weeks later on a scheduled report.
It was flagged here at +12% on 9/17 on the original Vertical Power Delivery license, and again Tuesday on the raise. Twice identified, never given an entry.
The fix is mechanical: if a name is worth two writeups, it is worth a level. “No usable level until the open prints one” is a description, not a plan.
COIN
Level tested and held · −1.25%
g
196.21 was named Monday and never traded until Wednesday. The low was 195.64 — through by 57 cents — and it closed 198.13, back above. First real test, held.
Premarket 195.65 is right back at it. Same plan, third day: a hold above 196.21 is the entry, a close below it ends the idea. The level has now earned its keep once.
Three sessions of patience for one test. Monday's gap-buyer at 204.31 is down 4.2%; the 196.21 buyer has not been filled badly once.
The SEC innovation exemption is still the catalyst and has not changed. What has changed is that bitcoin's run cooled and the froth came out.
This is what the discipline looks like when it works. It looked like a missed green day on Monday and it is a defined-risk entry on Thursday.
XOM
Second miss · +1.08%
y
“Not a long here” at 158.30. It bottomed 155.85 Tuesday and closed Wednesday 161.23, and is 162.98 now. The break was called right and the bounce was missed.
161.23 is the line it reclaimed. Holding above it, the three-session flush is over. USO +1.32% confirms — crude has turned with it.
The Failed 2D call was correct twice: the stack failed when crude broke $100, and XOM broke 161.31 on schedule. Then the analysis stopped at “not a long.”
Same error as VICR. A correct directional read with no level on the other side of it is only half a plan, and the half that does not make money.
Iran may still reopen Hormuz within seven days. The diplomacy that broke crude is unresolved, so this bounce is inside an unfinished story.
MGM
Deal withdrawn · −10.15%
r
Barry Diller's People Incorporated withdrew its acquisition proposal. Diller: “We didn't feel the mix was coming together in the way we had hoped” — and he still holds 66.8M shares.
No trade on a withdrawn-deal gap. The arb premium comes out in one print and the floor is wherever the standalone business is valued. Let it find that before marking a level.
The board is backing MGM's standalone plan, which is the part that matters: this is not a broken company, it is a removed bid.
A buyer holding 66.8M shares who walks away from control is a different signal than a seller. He is still long, just not buying the rest.
Watch where it stops. A withdrawn deal usually retraces to roughly the pre-rumour price, and that is the only level with any logic behind it.
SNX
Earnings · −10.38%
r
−10.38% on its report, one of the larger single-name breaks on the board alongside SFIX −17% and DRI −2.66%.
No trade into a fresh earnings gap with no level. Same rule as VKTX Monday: the session has to build a range before there is anything to trade against.
SNX is IT distribution, so it reads through to the hardware complex. Worth watching whether SMCI, DELL and HPE care — SMCI is −2.68% premarket.
DRI is the one to note for the record: EPS $2.05 in line, revenue $3.20B against $3.21B expected, full-year guidance reaffirmed — and it is down anyway.
In line plus reaffirmed plus down is a valuation reaction, not a results one. That is a tape telling you what it is willing to pay, and it applies to COST tonight.

darkpool.note: No fresh single-name tape for this session. What still stands from Friday's expiration board is the record: SPCX $9.4B at the ask, the largest single-name print this board has shown, and $18.7B cumulative (ask) ahead of NVDA $8.7B and AAPL $7.6B — all three top names on the same side. Ten single names printed $1B or more. The one lean price has since confirmed is energy, and it has now confirmed in both directions: XOM $1.2B and CVX $1.1B both printed at the ask as WTI slid toward $100, the flush ran three more sessions, and crude has now turned with USO +1.32% and XOM back above 161.23. Size marked the move and not its end — which is the useful distinction, because a side tells you who was in a hurry, not how far it goes. Treat the rest of that board loosely: it was a quad-witching flush and this book has two standing reminders of what over-reading a side costs. STX's mid print, called bearish into +6.93%. META's candle, called over its catalyst into +11.34%. Both entries stay on the page.
darkpool.right_note: Still open from Friday: ECHO $150P 12/18/26 at $8.6M, a floor put to December, and PANW $360C 09/25, the board's largest sweep, which expires tomorrow. Worth watching whether PANW gets marked into it. MU's $1000C dated 10/02 is deep in the money with the stock at 1,071.88 and the print landing 9/30 — the sweep that was placed two days past the earnings date is now the trade of the month on this board.
